transcript.text: Good evening everyone. I've called this meeting to close out the Bay 4 hydrogen alarm incident so we can get overnight charging capacity lined up. As we all know, Bay 4 sounded a hydrogen alarm during the afternoon shift, the alarm has since reset with no visible damage, and we need charging capacity for six forklifts tonight. I can authorize temporary use of Bay 2, which is normally reserved for maintenance vehicles. Before I can authorize charging, I need to hear a facilities maintenance report and an EHS report. Once I've heard both, I'll record the operating plan and assign follow-up actions. Let's get started — could I get the facilities maintenance report first?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: Here's the facilities maintenance report on Bay 4. I inspected Bay 4 after the alarm and found that the exhaust-fan belt has failed. The replacement belt is on site, but fitting and testing it will take exactly 6 hours. I haven't entered the emergency work order yet because the maintenance system was offline during the inspection.

transcript.text: Here's the EHS report. My same-day EHS review found that the Bay 4 alarm was caused by hydrogen accumulation. I also confirmed that Bay 2 is approved for no more than 4 simultaneous forklift chargers — not the 6 we need tonight. Additionally, our charging policy requires a 2-hour fire watch and a gas test showing less than 1% hydrogen before any charging can resume. I haven't attached the review to the incident record yet because the shift handover is still open.

Complete the 6-hour belt replacement and confirm ventilation fan is operational and tested before Bay 4 is returned to charging service.
Attach the same-day EHS review to the incident record once the shift handover is closed.
Conduct the 2-hour fire watch and gas test showing less than 1% hydrogen before any charging resumes in Bay 4.

Authorize temporary use of Bay 2 for up to 4 simultaneous forklift chargers tonight. Two of the six forklifts cannot be charged until Bay 4 is restored or additional capacity is identified. Bay 4 remains out of service until the exhaust-fan belt is replaced, ventilation is tested, fire watch is completed, and hydrogen gas test passes.
